function.mechanism: Used as an antimicrobial preservative to inhibit microbial growth in food systems.
common_food_categories: General foods under GMP in the US (maximum current GMP level 0.1% in food)
Historically liquid dietary supplements in the EU before withdrawal

adi.basis: EFSA (2004) did not include propyl p-hydroxybenzoate in the paraben group ADI; group ADI 0-10 mg/kg bw/day applied to methyl/ethyl parabens and their sodium salts.

efsa.key_finding: Propyl paraben should not be included in the group ADI due to concerns from reproductive-endpoint data in juvenile male rats.

adi.basis: WHO/JECFA database lists ADI as WITHDRAWN (2006); historical group ADI context included 0-10 mg/kg bw/day.

notable_bans: European Union: E216 withdrawn from authorized food additives framework via Directive 2006/52/EC.

concerns.summary: EFSA/JECFA identified reproductive-endpoint concern for propyl paraben, including adverse effects in male rat reproductive tissues at doses within the historical paraben group ADI range.

Recent animal studies report developmental, reproductive, and immunotoxic effects (mouse prenatal ovarian reserve effects; zebrafish developmental and immune-axis effects) with oxidative stress and signaling-pathway involvement.

Mechanistic and cell-model studies suggest potential procarcinogenic pathway activation and enhanced invasion in specific cancer models, but these data are not sufficient alone for human carcinogenic classification.

no_concern_confirmed: A recent human cohort analysis reported sex-specific and mixed behavioral associations, not uniformly adverse for propylparaben across strata.
IARC classification list did not identify propylparaben as a classified carcinogenic agent.

populations: Children (historical EU high consumers, especially users of food supplements)
Users of products combining multiple paraben exposure sources
adi_exceedance.notes: EU recital text reported temporary ADI exceedance scenarios in children (including up to 16% above temporary ADI for one supplement scenario, and larger exceedance scenarios in high consumers).

risk_assessment.rationale: Regulatory weight of evidence is cautionary: EFSA did not support propyl inclusion in the paraben group ADI, JECFA later withdrew ADI for propyl paraben, and the EU withdrew E216 authorization. FDA GRAS status remains, but does not outweigh the combined international regulatory concern profile.
key_factors: EFSA 2004 conclusion against including propyl in group ADI
Historical child exceedance concerns in EU recitals
Recent mechanistic/animal studies indicating endocrine-reproductive and other toxicity pathways
